RETURN", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u061-b0123", "target": "— Будущая, смею думать, устроится без особой оглядки на них, — возразил я. — А что они делают в отношении этой?", "source_sha256": "8c206e36a12e44c7d2ca7157101999b046db27c42700abdbf28240599e3cf8bf", "target_id": "ru-en85-u061-b0123", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "c650c7e1fb2a3fed9638763db25d8ba26bc7ccf1fa3a4caca08ef9401025ce45"}, {"source_id": "en85-u061-b0124", "target": "Мистер Чиллип покачал головой, помешал негус и отпил глоток.", "source_sha256": "b6fd51a75f026f5fa853c51290e871b219c450f3dfb45fa314aa5bf6ca7c791c", "target_id": "ru-en85-u061-b0124", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a231ef2c94901fb85b8abf6aff605d923bc593af4110f021312db1500336b8c2"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 59, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u061-b0125", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘She was a charming woman, sir!’ he observed in a plaintive manner.", "sha256": "421cc38d670686a5177b9c5ab72d6adb21f53161217f188858393d7f50edfff6", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[125]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0126", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘The present Mrs. Murdstone?’", "sha256": "bb057bf56375565ba3698193028c4abe69bad1a7e97a29b0f4ff5b96127d589d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[126]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0127", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘A charming woman indeed, sir,’ said Mr. Chillip; ‘as amiable, I am sure, as it was possible to be! Mrs. Chillip’s opinion is, that her spirit has been entirely broken since her marriage, and that she is all but melancholy mad. And the ladies,’ observed Mr. Chillip, timorously, ‘are great observers, sir.’", "sha256": "5b7e820273197a46dc18cd3f0c6fdeef6289371758a9bd1af793b6dbede31c74", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[127]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0128", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I suppose she was to be subdued and broken to their detestable mould, Heaven help her!’ said I. ‘And she has been.’", "sha256": "6f6301593cb244af0bb43b2a31873b7cc05d81f2aecf321b2233d6cd736a78e5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[128]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0129", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well, sir, there were violent quarrels at first, I assure you,’ said Mr. Chillip; ‘but she is quite a shadow now. Would it be considered forward if I was to say to you, sir, in confidence, that since the sister came to help, the brother and sister between them have nearly reduced her to a state of imbecility?’", "sha256": "406f3ed63c79ea9d323d8ef0640d85ee75fb448b59b2101a06a7d7ae6eb769d0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[129]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0130", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I told him I could easily believe it.", "sha256": "f187fff8e8b0e57ec605e2e547ce167887c65fea42a896f7ee991d7ac84b4e03", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[130]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0131", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I have no hesitation in saying,’ said Mr. Chillip, fortifying himself with another sip of negus, ‘between you and me, sir, that her mother died of it—or that tyranny, gloom, and worry have made Mrs. Murdstone nearly imbecile. She was a lively young woman, sir, before marriage, and their gloom and austerity destroyed her. They go about with her, now, more like her keepers than her husband and sister-in-law. That was Mrs. Chillip’s remark to me, only last week. And I assure you, sir, the ladies are great observers. Mrs. Chillip herself is a great observer!’", "sha256": "e808605c6c84f8afd7b513809bded75f68e34d9137cf7ce4227abc2b85f1d377", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[131]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0132", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Does he gloomily profess to be (I am ashamed to use the word in such association) religious still?’ I inquired.", "sha256": "2ca7f4d7bd6abd56bdb8c71bf9926f1ba8229727b6af4ff87847196cfe33ac7b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[132]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0133", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You anticipate, sir,’ said Mr. Chillip, his eyelids getting quite red with the unwonted stimulus in which he was indulging. ‘One of Mrs. Chillip’s most impressive remarks. Mrs. Chillip,’ he proceeded, in the calmest and slowest manner, ‘quite electrified me, by pointing out that Mr. Murdstone sets up an image of himself, and calls it the Divine Nature. You might have knocked me down on the flat of my back, sir, with the feather of a pen, I assure you, when Mrs. Chillip said so. The ladies are great observers, sir?’", "sha256": "5a46eda6bb6482e3769769b43b7d95d455e9be9d5e6a37655301453ae791988b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[133]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0134", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Intuitively,’ said I, to his extreme delight.", "sha256": "6a3ce922aee96294e5465d8defff428771e06f297ea8ed8215a0fcfefa64e735", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[134]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0135", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am very happy to receive such support in my opinion, sir,’ he rejoined. ‘It is not often that I venture to give a non-medical opinion, I assure you. Mr. Murdstone delivers public addresses sometimes, and it is said,—in short, sir, it is said by Mrs. Chillip,—that the darker tyrant he has lately been, the more ferocious is his doctrine.’", "sha256": "7aaceb49d248fdc31a44803700572c4b65f8b557ab43c6a8d296032efc436145", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[135]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0136", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I believe Mrs. Chillip to be perfectly right,’ said I.", "sha256": "cb21067f689152ed12107a6bec86226426981d84a1964c6ec9e58b25a167433b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[136]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0137", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mrs. Chillip does go so far as to say,’ pursued the meekest of little men, much encouraged, ‘that what such people miscall their religion, is a vent for their bad humours and arrogance. And do you know I must say, sir,’ he continued, mildly laying his head on one side, ‘that I DON’T find authority for Mr. and Miss Murdstone in the New Testament?’", "sha256": "9fa90bb0377aac5cf957c6d8d488ed06346e04fe54a9e416d275b74de1895338", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[137]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0138", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I never found it either!’ said I.", "sha256": "33f713b49c570f26b8669c59e362dbcfc3085b3cf0c3d08dcb0f1c593aa2f098", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[138]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0139", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘In the meantime, sir,’ said Mr. Chillip, ‘they are much disliked; and as they are very free in consigning everybody who dislikes them to perdition, we really have a good deal of perdition going on in our neighbourhood! However, as Mrs. Chillip says, sir, they undergo a continual punishment; for they are turned inward, to feed upon their own hearts, and their own hearts are very bad feeding. Now, sir, about that brain of yours, if you’ll excuse my returning to it. Don’t you expose it to a good deal of excitement, sir?’", "sha256": "4372c53f529e7095acfbcc3fb622bdd90ddfeb157c402c69fdb12f8140aa4229", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[139]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0140", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I found it not difficult, in the excitement of Mr. Chillip’s own brain, under his potations of negus, to divert his attention from this topic to his own affairs, on which, for the next half-hour, he was quite loquacious; giving me to understand, among other pieces of information, that he was then at the Gray’s Inn Coffee-house to lay his professional evidence before a Commission of Lunacy, touching the state of mind of a patient who had become deranged from excessive drinking. ‘And I assure you, sir,’ he said, ‘I am extremely nervous on such occasions. I could not support being what is called Bullied, sir. It would quite unman me. Do you know it was some time before I recovered the conduct of that alarming lady, on the night of your birth, Mr. Copperfield?’", "sha256": "5c590f6554c1b5d0a0688da768b6109cc8905ce1e7d0375daf231bf30721a5b7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[140]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0141", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I told him that I was going down to my aunt, the Dragon of that night, early in the morning; and that she was one of the most tender-hearted and excellent of women, as he would know full well if he knew her better. The mere notion of the possibility of his ever seeing her again, appeared to terrify him. He replied with a small pale smile, ‘Is she so, indeed, sir? Really?’ and almost immediately called for a candle, and went to bed, as if he were not quite safe anywhere else. He did not actually stagger under the negus; but I should think his placid little pulse must have made two or three more beats in a minute, than it had done since the great night of my aunt’s disappointment, when she struck at him with her bonnet.", "sha256": "0ff57825cdf0ab1ee4aec159dbd68801e50a34703b09325d6c88995cde846b79", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[141]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u061-b0142", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Thoroughly tired, I went to bed too, at midnight; passed the next day on the Dover coach; burst safe and sound into my aunt’s old parlour while she was at tea (she wore spectacles now); and was received by her, and Mr. Dick, and dear old Peggotty, who acted as housekeeper, with open arms and tears of joy. My aunt was mightily amused, when we began to talk composedly, by my account of my meeting with Mr. Chillip, and of his holding her in such dread remembrance; and both she and Peggotty had a great deal to say about my poor mother’s second husband, and ‘that murdering woman of a sister’,—on whom I think no pain or penalty would have induced my aunt to bestow any Christian or Proper Name, or any other designation.", "sha256": "cb618fd0bb4ec8cdf898eb4dd838e727e0ec630c2ca90a17a1b614959c881dce", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[66]/p[142]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
